# Lunar Scenario Explorer, the map

This file is the back of the tapestry. It records what the app holds and how the app is wired, so
that an agent unable to hold the artifact in one context can still see the whole picture without
re-deriving it. The front of the tapestry is the app. Nothing here is authority. Everything here is
derived from the app and from the two registers, and the app is where a disagreement is settled.

## This file is generated, and a hand edit to it fails

Do not edit this file. It is written by `tools/build_map.js` and regeneration reproduces it byte for byte.
The reason is the standing rule this step turns on: a reference a machine cannot follow is a copy, and
a copy drifts. Hand-written, this map would be the largest copy the project has ever made, and it
would sit inside the step whose whole purpose is retiring second authorities. Generated, it cannot
disagree with the app without the disagreement being loud.

```
node tools/build_map.js            rewrite this file from the artifact
node tools/build_map.js --check    prove the file on disk is what the artifact generates
node tools/build_map.js --prove    prove the instrument, its known answers and its 6 decoys
```

The check reads this file as bytes, regenerates in memory, and compares. A hand edit anywhere in the
file, including in this paragraph, makes it exit non-zero and print the offset of the first differing
byte. That is the decoy the design is built to catch, and it is why the map can be trusted without
being read end to end.

## Provenance, and the two stamps are not the same kind of thing

| item | value | kind of stamp |
|---|---|---|
| Source artifact | `index.html` | the app in this repository |
| Artifact md5 | `9574f0b21be67c2bc0625175d1fe4e69` | DERIVED. The generator reads the file and derives the digest at this build. It holds no expected value to compare against, since the pin was removed so the generator runs against any build on any machine |
| Artifact bytes on disk | 889,683 | measured at this build |
| Data island pin | `f95dfeaa` | RECORDED OBSERVATION. Read out of the artifact. It is FNV-1a over CONFIG, CLAIMS, VALUE and LANDED_COST, and there is nothing here to compare it against |
| Generator | `tools/build_map.js` | this file names it and it names this file |

Neither stamp is a check, and that is a change from how this file used to read. The generator
derives the digest from whatever file it is pointed at and holds no expected value to compare
it against, so a wrong artifact produces a map describing that artifact rather than a refusal.
The pin is read out of the artifact the same way. Both are measurements of what was built, and
what makes them useful is that they name the build rather than that they guard it.

| State blurbs | 20 | a scenario cell with prose |
| Sections with a blurb still pending | 12 | declared pending rather than silently absent |
| References | 63 | a source entry |

| References no section cites | 6 | measured backward |
| Retired identifiers with a resolved slug | 63 | an old number-label and what it became |
| Retired identifiers resolved by adjudication | 3 | resolved with the reason recorded |
| Retired identifiers nothing decides | 1 | recorded unresolved rather than assigned by proximity |
| Registered artifacts | 24 | a row in the artifact register |
| Artifacts a builder produces | 9 | a derived copy with a machine-followable join |
| Registered artifacts present at their registered path | 24 | measured against the disk at this build |
| Registered artifacts absent from their registered path | 0 | a register-against-disk divergence, listed below |
| Declared manual dependencies | 13 | a restatement with no builder, each verified present at this build |

The slug total and the heading total are not reconcilable to each other and are not meant to be. A
heading attaches to display and a slug attaches to anything a link can point at. Two headings each
cover nine per-cell sections, so nine addressable things sit under one heading in two places.

The SECTIONS object is built at load time by aliasing the leaves of CLAIMS, so its members are the
same objects by reference rather than copies of them. Any walk over the island that does not exclude
it counts every claim string twice. This generator excludes it by construction and proves the
aliasing is real rather than assuming it.

## Where each rendered value comes from

The equations the Equations tab prints, each with the sections that license it.

| symbol | expression | licensed by |
|---|---|---|
| `eEE` | e(ice) = E1 / ice | `energy-per-tonne`, `bilinear-water-law` |
| `rho` | rho = 100 / ice | `polar-cold-trap-water`, `bilinear-water-law` |
| `Wpower` | W_power = power * H * duty / e(ice) | `energy-per-tonne` |
| `mPwr` | M_power = f_pwr * power + (transmission/1000) * transDistKm * power | `fission-specific-power`, `solar-mass-allocation`, `zero-intercept-mass-law` |
| `massEff` | M_eff = mass * (1 - phi_c0) | `shared-capacity-split` |
| `mining` | M_mining = max(0, M_eff - M_power) | `zero-intercept-mass-law` |
| `Rcap` | R_cap = kExc * M_mining | `throughput-coefficient` |
| `Wthr` | W_thr = (R_cap / rho) * captureEff | `capture-derate`, `min-of-two-limits` |
| `cap` | cap = min(W_power, W_thr) | `min-of-two-limits`, `binding-regime-labels` |
| `water` | water = (1 - phi_c) * cap | `shared-capacity-split` |
| `Cfull` | C_full = min(power * H * duty / e_sinter, Y_sinter * R_cap) | `sintering-specific-energy`, `sintering-yield` |
| `construction` | construction = phi_c * C_full | `shared-capacity-split`, `water-primary-default` |
| `r_prop` | r_prop = mass / (cap * L) | `amortized-plant-identity`, `shared-capacity-split`, `industrial-plant-price` |
| `r_const` | r_const = mass / (C_full * L) | `amortized-plant-identity`, `shared-capacity-split`, `industrial-plant-price` |
| `P` | P = r * D + op | `industrial-plant-price`, `propellant-operating-floor` |
| `margin` | margin = D - P = D * (1 - r) - op | `industrial-plant-price`, `propellant-operating-floor`, `ladder-range-and-floor` |
| `value` | value = rate * 1000 * margin | `industrial-plant-price` |
| `ranking` | ranking = C_full / cap = r_prop / r_const | `product-payback-ranking` |
| `Dstar` | D* = op_prop / (1 - r_prop) | `product-payback-ranking`, `propellant-operating-floor` |

that is simply missing cannot say why it is missing, and a reader meeting a gap has no way to tell a
ruling from an oversight.

## What this map leaves out, and why

Three sections of this map are omitted from the published build. They describe how this
project files and rebuilds its own working copies: which deliverable derives from which, where
each registered artifact sits on a working disk, and which documents restate a coefficient the
app owns. All three are about a working tree that is not in this repository, so a reader here
could not act on any of them, and two of them name folders and filenames that do not ship.

Nothing about the app is omitted. Every section above is generated from the artifact itself.

## What this map does not do

It holds no figure as authority. Every number above was read out of the artifact at the build named at
the top of this file, and the artifact is where a disagreement is settled.

It does not check that a link target supports the sentence pointing at it. A bracketed slug that
resolves is a reference a machine can follow, which is the whole of what the resolution check claims.
Whether the section at the other end actually supports the assertion is a reading question, and no
check in this generator reaches it.

It does not rank, score or judge. A tier and a state are read off the artifact and reprinted. Where
this file says a node is excluded, that is the register speaking rather than this file.
